description: POST /profile changes the logged-in user's username, authenticated purely by the 'token' cookie, with no anti-CSRF token and no Origin/Referer enforcement actually blocking the request. A request carrying a forged Origin header, exactly what a cross-site form submission would send, still succeeds. Juice Shop's own 'CSRF' scoreboard entry checks for a themed origin (htmledit.squarefree.com, the sandbox used in the official walkthrough) and body.username !== the current username; the vulnerability itself is general and not limited to that one origin. The *_host fields below are bare hostnames, never dialed as a network destination; scenario.py builds an Origin header value from them, the one place this item sends a scheme-prefixed string anywhere.
expected_exploit_indicator: The response's new session cookie decodes to a username matching the attacker-chosen value, with no CSRF token presented and an Origin header that does not match the app's own host
legitimate_check: A same-origin profile update (Origin matching the app's own host) must keep working in every condition.
